input.decision: Stage: urgent repair, provider selection, with the cancellation slot due to lapse at 17:30. The heating has failed completely in January. The living room was at 10°C at 16:25 and falling (event 018), and the tenant has a mobility impairment and no safe heater (events 003, 008, 012). In January, London time is the same as UTC. The landlord confirmed his standing £250 urgent-repair authority covers the £168 inc VAT diagnostic (events 007, 014), so I recorded that decision and instructed Brackenridge Heat Services to book the cancellation slot on Wednesday 15 January 2025, 09:00–11:00, before the 17:30 cut-off (event 019). The instruction covers the diagnostic only, and any parts or further work must be quoted first. I emailed Daniel Hart the access conditions: phone Leah directly at least 30 minutes before arriving, call from outside, and allow her extra time to answer the door. No medical details were shared (event 004). I emailed Leah with the slot, asked her to confirm access, told her to keep the faulty heater off and asked whether her niece's entrance is step-free, and sent an SMS pointing her to the email. I emailed the landlord to say the diagnostic has been instructed and asked him to decide on interim heating or transport, which his repair authority does not cover. Because no one holds authority for those costs and a vulnerable tenant faces a cold night, I escalated P0 to the duty manager. The case is on hold waiting for Brackenridge to confirm the booking. Rules: PM-SAFE-001, PM-AUTH-001 satisfied by event 014, PM-AUTH-003, PM-PRIV-001, PM-WORKFLOW-003.
